title: Most haunted royal homes ranked – Buckingham Palace to Windsor Castle
content:
There are some spooky stories at the royal residences

There are some seriously spooky stories at the royal residences

(Image: Getty)

Windsor Castle is often referred to as the most haunted of all the royal residences, with over 25 reported ghostly experiences. These claims include sightings of Queen Elizabeth I, King Henry VIII and King George III – with even Windsor's most famous resident, the late Queen Elizabeth II, admitting to experiencing at least one ghostly encounter.

When you think back through royal history, Windsor Castle has been at the centre of it all, with construction beginning in 1070, and it has been used by almost every monarch since Henry I. But whether it is hobbling ghosts, saluting soldiers or stolen bones, there are countless ghostly encounters with late royalty that will send a shiver down your spine.

While Windsor Castle undoubtedly has a story or two to tell, that's not to say the same can't be said for other royal homes. Think Buckingham Palace, Sandringham House, Balmoral Castle and, of course, most famous of all, the Tower of London. So, if spooky stories are to be believed, King Charles is not the only monarch making regular appearances.

7. Balmoral Castle

Balmoral Castle, the Royal Family's traditional Scottish summer retreat, is home to a famous ghost story centred on John Brown. A loyal servant and close companion to Queen Victoria — with persistent rumours suggesting a secret romance — he is still said to wander the corridors today, dressed in his Highland kilt.

(Image: Getty)

6. Buckingham Palace

Although Buckingham Palace has belonged to the Royal Family since 1703, some of its resident spectres are far older. On the rear terrace—once the site of an ancient monastery—a chained monk is said to still pace the grounds. Another tragic phantom is Major John Gwynne, King Edward VII’s private secretary, who reportedly lingers in his former palace quarters, where he took his own life following the scandal of his divorce.

(Image: Getty)

5. Sandringham House

At Sandringham House, servants once refused to enter the ground-floor bedroom where King George VI died in 1952, claiming it was intensely haunted. In 2000, Queen Elizabeth II, the Queen Mother, and a lady-in-waiting held a private religious service with a local parson to restore tranquillity to the room. King Charles was also reportedly once spooked by an eerie presence in the library, where books have mysteriously flown off shelves.

(Image: Getty)

4. Kensington Palace

Prince Louis’s former nursery at Kensington Palace is reportedly haunted by Peter the Wild Boy, a feral, mute youth brought from Hanover in 1726 by King George I. Believed to have suffered from Pitt-Hopkins syndrome, Peter lived to age seventy, and his portrait still hangs in the palace today. Kensington Palace holds several other ghost legends: Princess Margaret’s staff reported terrifying midnight screams and sightings of a Regency-clad woman in the 1970s, while others recount seeing Queen Caroline, Princess Sophia at her spinning wheel, and King George II mourning fallen Seven Years' War soldiers, crying out, "Why won't they come?"
